lootRule: When an enemy is defeated the narrator rolls 1d6: if odd the first loot item drops; if even the second loot item drops.

difficultyTable.label: Very Easy
difficultyTable.example: Picking up a dropped item in an open space, walking across a solid bridge without distractions.

difficultyTable.label: Easy
difficultyTable.example: Retrieving a dropped item near a ledge, recalling basic information from a scroll.

difficultyTable.label: Moderate
difficultyTable.example: Climbing a tree for a better view, calming an irritated NPC, picking a simple lock.

difficultyTable.label: Hard
difficultyTable.example: Grabbing a dangling rope from a ledge, sneaking past a guard, disarming a basic trap.

difficultyTable.label: Very Hard
difficultyTable.example: Scaling a sheer wall in the rain, hacking into a basic security system under time pressure.

difficultyTable.label: Difficult
difficultyTable.example: Running across a slick slope, navigating a maze of collapsing ruins, retrieving a relic from ruins.

difficultyTable.label: Very Difficult
difficultyTable.example: Battling a powerful arcane creature, convincing a faction leader to give away key information.

difficultyTable.label: Nearly Impossible
difficultyTable.example: Defeating a heavily armored foe with a dagger, swimming through raging currents.

difficultyTable.label: Impossible
difficultyTable.example: Running through a barrage of attacks unscathed, lifting a huge boulder in an adrenaline rush.

difficultyTable.label: Legendary
difficultyTable.example: Surviving a fall from a great height with last-second intervention, battling an ancient arcane entity.
